text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Exports of Dutch manufactured goods rose eight percent in October compared with same month of 1995. (p1)
- President Chirac of France agrees to joint EU action on drugs despite strong reservations about Dutch drugs policy. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank gets approval from Federal Reserve Board to take over U.S. investment bank Chicago Corporation. (p3)
- Chip tester Rood Technology says it will post a loss for second half of 1996. (p3)
- Cabinet backs plans to hold auction for a third national mobile telecommunications licence based on DCS technology. (p3)
- Dutch steel maker Hoogovens to discuss planned participation in Belgian steel company Boel with Walloon regional government this week. (p4)
- Generale Bank Nederland to form an alliance with Elvia, a subsidiary of Germany's insurer Allianz. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- New European Union treaty might not be finalised during Dutch tenure of rotating EU presidency. (p1)
- Filmnet's parent company Nethold to experiment with new service to provide pay-per-view movie service. (p2)
- Half of Dutch firms of architects is loss-making, according to professional association BNA. (p2)
- LCI Computer group takes over Rotterdam-based automation firm System Plus. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Family doctors want government compensation for transfer of 200,000 elderly people from private to public health insurance. (p1)
- Dutch national soccer team beats Belgium 3-0 in World Cup qualification match. (p1)
- Airlines Martinair and Air Holland compete for rights to
operate flights to Indonesia. (p4)
TROUW
- Netherlands participates in new United Nations rapid reaction military force. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Dutch composer Tristan Keuris dies at 50. (p1)
- Future looks gloomy for small supermarkets, according to trade journal Distrifood. (p9)
